Job Description: The Senior Project Development Manager – Energy Storage Technologies role at Ferrovial Energy is responsible for originating, developing, evaluating, acquiring, and advancing utility-scale energy storage opportunities across the U.S. and Canada. The role will focus on a broad range of storage technologies, including lithium-ion battery storage, thermal storage, iron-based storage, vanadium redox flow batteries, and other emerging short-duration and long-duration energy storage solutions. The position will support standalone storage, renewable-plus-storage hybrid projects, behind-the-meter and front-of-the-meter applications, data center energy infrastructure solutions, and other strategic storage opportunities aligned with Ferrovial Energy’s growth objectives. The position will be based at the Ferrovial Energy US headquarters in Austin, TX, and reports to the Director, Project Development. You will work closely with the U.S. Development team, finance, M&A, engineering, commercial, legal, construction, asset management, and corporate strategy teams. The Senior Manager will identify and secure new sites, evaluate technology and market opportunities, lead commercial and technical due diligence, support acquisitions and partnership structures, build relationships with technology providers and developers, and prepare executive-level materials for investment decisions, business planning, and management updates. The goal is to build a differentiated energy storage pipeline that supports grid reliability, renewable integration, customer load growth, data center power needs, and long-term value creation for Ferrovial Energy. RESPONSIBILITIES Serve as project lead for standalone energy storage, hybrid renewable-plus-storage, and data center-related energy infrastructure opportunities, coordinating internal cross-functional teams and external consultants across development, interconnection, permitting, land, engineering, finance, legal, commercial, construction, and asset management workstreams. Originate, screen, and advance energy storage projects across multiple technologies, including lithium-ion batteries, thermal storage, iron-based storage, vanadium redox flow batteries, and other emerging short-duration and long-duration storage solutions. Evaluate market applications for storage projects, including resource adequacy, capacity, ancillary services, congestion management, renewable integration, curtailment mitigation, resiliency, microgrids, tolling structures, data center power solutions, and customer-specific energy needs. Lead site identification and project development activities, including land control, permitting strategy, environmental review, stakeholder outreach, community engagement, utility coordination, interconnection strategy, transmission review, and project schedule management. Support commercial, technical, and financial modeling for storage projects, including revenue forecasts, dispatch assumptions, market participation strategies, degradation and augmentation assumptions, lifecycle cost analysis, CAPEX/OPEX estimates, tax credit sensitivity, and investment case preparation. Prepare executive-level briefings, business updates, investment committee materials, project memoranda, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations for senior and executive management. Support M&A, project acquisition, co-development, and joint venture opportunities by leading or contributing to due diligence, valuation inputs, transaction structuring, development risk assessment, technology review, and negotiation support. Develop and manage strategic partnerships with technology suppliers, developers, utilities, load-serving entities, data center customers, EPC contractors, engineering firms, consultants, landowners, public agencies, and financial partners. Prepare, review, and manage requests for information, proposals, bids, technology evaluations, owner’s engineer scopes, and consultant work products related to energy storage development and execution. Coordinate project handoff and continuity from development into financing, procurement, construction, commissioning, operations, asset management, and long-term performance monitoring. Track storage technology trends, policy developments, ISO/RTO market rules, utility requirements, interconnection reforms, data center load growth, and evolving commercial structures for short-duration and long-duration storage. Participate in industry conferences, technology roundtables, customer meetings, and partner discussions to build market intelligence, identify opportunities, and strengthen Ferrovial Energy’s visibility in the storage sector. Manage assigned project budgets, objectives, schedules, development milestones, risk registers, consultant scopes, and internal reporting obligations. Support, mentor, and coordinate more junior development managers, associates, analysts, and consultants working on assigned projects and strategic initiatives. Promote a culture of safety, integrity, respect, accountability, collaboration, and commercial discipline across all project activities. REQUIREMENTS Engineering, finance, economics, business, environmental, or other relevant degree preferred; equivalent experience in energy storage, power infrastructure, project development, or investment analysis will be considered. Minimum of 6 to 9 years of relevant experience in energy storage, renewable energy, power generation, infrastructure development, IPP, utility, EPC, consulting, investment, or project acquisition roles. Required experience with utility-scale energy storage development, including standalone storage and hybrid renewable-plus-storage projects; experience with data center energy infrastructure, behind-the-meter solutions, microgrids, or large-load power solutions preferred. Strong understanding of short-duration and long-duration energy storage technologies, including lithium-ion BESS, thermal storage, iron-based storage, vanadium redox flow batteries, and other emerging storage technologies. Experience developing, acquiring, financing, or evaluating storage projects across the full lifecycle, from origination, market screening, land, interconnection, permitting, and stakeholder outreach through financing, construction readiness, commissioning, and operations support. Demonstrated ability to prepare and interpret project financial models, market models, dispatch scenarios, lifecycle cost comparisons, revenue forecasts, sensitivity analyses, and investment materials for storage assets. Required experience supporting M&A, project acquisitions, co-development structures, joint ventures, partnerships, or strategic investments in energy storage, renewables, data centers, or adjacent energy infrastructure sectors. Ability to prepare clear, concise, and commercially oriented materials for executive management, including investment committee presentations, management updates, project approvals, risk summaries, and strategic recommendations. Strong knowledge of U.S. interconnection and transmission processes across multiple ISO/RTO and utility markets, including queue strategy, grid constraints, congestion, curtailment, capacity markets, ancillary services, storage revenue opportunities, and market-specific rules in regions such as ERCOT, SPP, MISO, PJM, CAISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, WECC, and SERC. Established network with storage technology providers, project developers, utilities, load-serving entities, commercial off-takers, data center customers, EPC contractors, consultants, land agents, public agencies, and financial partners preferred. Strong stakeholder outreach and communication skills, with the ability to engage landowners, community leaders, local officials, regulators, utilities, customers, industry groups, internal executive stakeholders, and cross-functional internal teams, including other project developers, engineers, EPC, construction, finance, legal, commercial, and asset management personnel. Commercially astute, proactive, collaborative, autonomous, flexible, and solutions-oriented, with the ability to manage competing priorities, anticipate risks, and drive projects forward in a dynamic market environment. Available to travel as required for project development, stakeholder meetings, technology diligence, partner engagement, site visits, conferences, and transaction-related activities. Lead decision‑making on data platform patterns, governance standards, and modernization initiatives. Mentor technical teams and drive adoption of best practices in cloud data engineering, DevOps, and Lakehouse architecture. Advanced hands‑on experience with ADF, Azure SQL, Synapse, and ADLS Gen2. Strong SQL Server background with performance tuning expertise. Experience with DB2/iSeries data structures and migration. Familiarity with Cosmos DB/NoSQL and Databricks/PySpark. Preferred Azure DevOps, CI/CD, and Infrastructure‑as‑Code (ARM/Bicep/Terraform). Azure Entra ID and least‑privilege security architecture. Azure cost governance and optimization. Strong experience with Microsoft Fabric. FleetPride is the leader in the industry comprised of retail, service, distribution and wholesale divisions. title: Credit Products Manager
jd_text: Position Title Credit Products Manager   Location Work From Home TX, TX 73301   Job Summary The Credit Products Manager (CPM) is responsible for overseeing first-line credit underwriting and portfolio management within an assigned business including but not limited to Corporate Banking and Regional Commercial Banking, ensuring alignment with the bank’s risk appetite and business objectives. This role manages a team of underwriters and credit professionals (Credit Products Specialists and Credit Products Analysts), ensuring accurate risk ratings, loan evaluation and underwriting, and ongoing portfolio management. Utilizing data-driven insights and portfolio analytics, a CPM identifies emerging risks and opportunities, providing recommendations to leadership to support sound credit decisions. Collaborating with sales, risk, and technology teams, this role helps drive responsible growth, improve underwriting processes, and enhance credit product offerings. With a focus on operational execution, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement, a CPM plays a key role in maintaining portfolio quality and supporting the bank’s long-term success.   Job Responsibilities: Maintains visibility and deep knowledge of bank relationships within the assigned LOB to ensure alignment with business objectives. Executes on the strategic priorities set by the Head of Credit Products, Line of Business leaders, Credit Products Senior Director and 2nd and 3rd Line Risk partners to ensure alignment with enterprise goals. Proactively identifies and escalates areas for improvement in credit processes, policies and procedures. Maintains the credit quality of assigned portfolios and/or lending verticals by overseeing underwriting, portfolio management, and risk monitoring activities. Establishes and fosters a shared vision across assigned regions and verticals, ensuring consistency in credit decisioning and risk management practices. Attracts, develops, and retains top talent within Credit Products by providing leadership, coaching, and professional development opportunities for underwriters, portfolio managers, and credit analysts. Collaborates closely with Sales, Credit Products, and Risk teams to drive responsible growth, optimize credit decisioning, and enhance portfolio performance. Serves as a key point of contact for deal flow assignment, credit risk reviews, and escalations, ensuring timely and well-informed credit decisions. Leverages data-driven insights and analytics to identify emerging credit risks and opportunities, proactively adjusting strategies as needed. Well versed in legal documentation (e.g., Credit Agreements) and positioned to both develop more junior associates on the topic and interact with internal and external legal counsel and negotiate terms directly with clients. Ensures compliance with regulatory requirements, internal policies, and risk frameworks while supporting continuous process improvements. Provides credit risk reporting and analysis to senior leadership, contributing to portfolio strategy and risk management discussions. Partners with legal and compliance teams to ensure underwriting and portfolio management practices align with all regulatory requirements. Supports senior leadership in delivering portfolio analysis and reporting, contributing to strategic decision-making. Recruits, develops and trains top credit underwriting and portfolio management talent. ADDITIONAL ACCOUNTABILITIES Performs special projects, to include continuous improvement and transformation initiatives, and additional duties and responsibilities as required. Consistently adheres to regulatory and compliance policies and standards linked to the job as listed and complete required compliance trainings. Accountable to maintain compliance with applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations. JOB REQUIREMENTS Preferred Qualifications: Undergraduate Degree (4 years or equivalent) in Business, Economics or related field and Master's Degree (or Postgraduate equivalent) . Minimum experience preferred: 12+ Years of 1st line of defense credit underwriting, portfolio management, and risk management experience within the Financial Industry including credit strategy and credit analytics. 5+ years of experience in managing teams of credit analysts, underwriters in the specialty vertical. 5+ years of experience in the direct specialized line of business (Specialized commercial industries, capital markets, corporate commercial banking, etc.) Experience and expertise in credit bureaus, credit decision engines, credit and cash flow modeling for underwriting and portfolio management decisions, income/identity verification and loss forecasting. Job Competencies: Strong knowledge of federal and state laws and regulations related to credit decisions, ensuring compliance in underwriting and portfolio management. For certain LOBs (e.g., Corporate Banking and Specialized Industries), a strong working knowledge of the syndicated loan market and related processes. Proficiency in credit bureaus, credit decision engines, underwriting models, and portfolio management strategies, with experience in income/identity verification and risk assessment. Effective communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate credit analysis into actionable strategies and policies for key stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to contribute to business strategy by incorporating industry knowledge and market trends into credit risk assessments and recommendations. Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and execute tasks efficiently in a fast-paced environment. Strong leadership and team development skills, fostering collaboration, coaching, and professional growth within the credit team. Physical demands (ADA): No unusual physical exertion is involved.
